title: Five hundred stone spires
text: The Trona Pinnacles are more than 500 tufa spires, some as high as 140 feet, rising from the bed of the Searles Lake basin. They formed underwater between 10,000 and 100,000 years ago, when Searles Lake was a link in a chain of interconnected lakes. The area was once under 640 feet of water, during the Pleistocene. A 5-mile dirt road leads to them, usually passable in a two-wheel-drive vehicle, though it may be closed after heavy rain.
